key.heading: Your OpenPGP key
key.none: You have no OpenPGP key registered here.
key.notHardware: This service cannot tell whether the key is on a security key's OpenPGP card or in a file, so it records neither.
register.heading: Register an OpenPGP key
register.intro: You prove the key is yours by signing a challenge with it. Its user ID must carry {mail}, the address on your account.
register.step1: Sign this text exactly as it is shown, before {at}. On a YubiKey or another OpenPGP card, the card signs it.
register.step2: For example, paste it into the first command below and paste what it prints into the second box; the second command prints your public key for the first box.
register.signed: The signed challenge (from -----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----)
wkd.heading: Web Key Directory
wkd.intro: Mail programs look up your public key at your mail domain's Web Key Directory so they can encrypt mail to you. You choose whether it is published.
wkd.off: This service does not publish a Web Key Directory for your organisation.
wkd.otherDomain: This service does not publish the Web Key Directory for your address's domain.
wkd.noKey: Register a key first to publish it.
mail.heading: Encrypted mail
mail.intro: Mail this service sends you can be encrypted to your OpenPGP key or to your S/MIME certificate. An encrypted message's subject only says what kind of message it is; the real subject is inside.
smime.heading: Your S/MIME certificate
smime.none: You have no S/MIME certificate here.
smime.unusable: The S/MIME certificate on your account cannot be used to encrypt mail now (it may have expired).
smime.paste: A certificate in PEM form, naming your address
done.challenge: Here is your challenge. Sign it and paste it below with your public key.
done.replaced: Your OpenPGP key {fingerprint} is registered and replaces the earlier one.
done.choiceReset: It has no encryption key, so your mail is no longer encrypted.
done.published: Your key is published in the Web Key Directory.
done.withdrawn: Your key is no longer published.
done.mail.openpgp: Your mail is now encrypted with your OpenPGP key.
done.mail.smime: Your mail is now encrypted with your S/MIME certificate.
